title: Identity Gatekeeper: urgent fix for RBAC + SAML group reconciliation causing audit gaps and KMS wrap failures
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise Private customers reported elevated privilege observations, missing audit entries for role changes, and intermittent failures encrypting audit blobs after a SAML group sync. Investigation shows a race between the SAML group reconciliation path and the local RBAC cache invalidation path; during a narrow window the system accepted transient grants but skipped emitting audit records, and a simultaneous KMS keywrap rotation path could fail to re-wrap recent audit blobs. Impact: 3 paying enterprise customers experienced incorrect effective permissions for 5-15 minutes during syncs and audit logs for those role changes were missing or stored unwrapped. This is a production security incident that requires an urgent patch and a coordinated postmortem and customer communication.
repro_steps: 1) Private deployment with SAML group mapping enabled and local RBAC enabled
2) Trigger SAML IdP group sync (simulate 1000+ group changes in a single sync job),
3) Concurrently trigger a key rotation for the KMS envelope key used by the audit pipeline
4) Observe: RBAC engine applies temporary grants before cache refresh completes; audit writer occasionally skips transactional flush when KMS wrap returns 403 on the rotate path

5) Result: some role-change events are not present in audit logs, and a handful of audit blobs were left with an older envelope key that did not match post-rotation metadata causing downstream indexers to drop them.
root_cause_analysis: The identity reconciliation code used a non-atomic path: SAML sync writes provisional role assignments to the database and emits an async cache-invalidate event. A subsequent request path could read the provisional assignments before the audit writer started its transaction. The audit writer assumed KMS envelope key availability and attempted an immediate keywrap; during scheduled rotations the KMS client could receive a transient unauthorized response (race during service principal token refresh) and bubbled an error that caused the transaction to roll back silently (error path not instrumented in production), leading to missing audit records. Two separate race windows combined to produce the customer-observed gap.
proposed_fix: A. Make SAML group reconciliation fully transactional: apply DB role changes and enqueue audit events in the same DB transaction (use transactional outbox pattern).
B. Add a short-lived in-process lock around identity reconcile + audit-write for the affected tenant to prevent interleaving with request-time reads (optimistic CAS with 5s backoff).

C. Harden KMS client: retry on token-refresh transient 401/403 with exponential backoff and fallback to the previous valid envelope key for wrap operations until rotation completes. Log and surface KMS rotation state to Console.
D. Add instrumentation: counters for "audit_event_dropped", per-tenant KMS rotation failures, and traces linking reconcile -> audit-write -> KMS wrap.
E. Add a migration to scan the last 72 hours of role-change events and reconcile missing audit entries (best-effort re-emit) for affected tenants.
F. Backport the minimal hotpatch to private-agent and runtime branches to support customers on older private releases.

rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotpatch to private-agent main and runtime-1.18 branch; run full CI with integration tests
2) Deploy to canary Private cluster (3 tenants) with increased logging and alerting for audit_event_dropped and KMS rotation errors
3) If canary green for 60m, schedule hotpatch deployment to impacted customers in maintenance windows and offer assisted upgrade
4) After customer upgrades, run the 72-hour audit reconciliation job for each tenant and verify re-emitted entries in Console audit UI
5) Post-deploy: monitor for 48h and run postmortem; prepare public incident summary and customer-facing notice.
